record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.original_question: Can the small beta-energy dependence of nuclear gamma-W-box radiative corrections be measured directly, and can such measurements benchmark theoretical estimates of nuclear Nachtmann-moment contributions when the expected slope is only a few parts in 10^-4 per MeV?

evidence.quote: It would be highly desirable to perform an experimental measurement of the energy dependence in parallel with theoretical estimates, but the smallness of the slope (on the order of a few parts in 10−4 per MeV) makes this extremely challenging.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In allowed nuclear beta decay, the differential decay rate as a function of the beta particle's kinetic energy E receives an electroweak radiative correction that includes a hadronic/nuclear gamma-W box contribution. This nuclear gamma-W box contribution carries a small dependence on E that, in current theoretical estimates based on dispersion representations involving the first Nachtmann moment of the γW interference structure function F_3, produces a slope of order a few parts in 10^{-4} per MeV in the energy-dependent correction factor multiplying the spectrum.

Determine whether the following is possible:

(a) Design and analyze an experimental procedure capable of directly detecting a slope of order 10^{-4} per MeV in the beta-energy-dependent nuclear gamma-W box radiative correction to the allowed beta spectrum, specifying the required precision, kinematic range, and systematic-error budget.

(b) Show how such a direct measurement of the energy-dependent slope can be used to benchmark (i.e., constrain or falsify) theoretical estimates of the nuclear Nachtmann-moment contributions that enter the dispersive computation of the gamma-W box, and quantify the level at which a measurement can discriminate between competing nuclear-structure inputs.

Equivalently: does there exist (in principle and in practice) a beta-spectrum measurement strategy whose statistical and systematic sensitivity is better than a few parts in 10^{-4} per MeV across the relevant beta endpoint range, sufficient to test current theoretical predictions for the energy slope of nuclear gamma-W box corrections?
artifact.category_tag: Electroweak radiative corrections in beta decay
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on radiative corrections to neutron and superallowed nuclear beta decay (e.g., dispersive analyses via Nachtmann moments of F_3, and updates of Δ_R^V) actively discuss the gamma-W box contribution and its uncertainties, but no published experiment has directly measured the predicted few-parts-in-10^{-4}-per-MeV beta-energy slope of the nuclear gamma-W box correction. The challenge is repeatedly described as extremely difficult, and no benchmarking measurement of the Nachtmann-moment-based estimates appears to exist as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Reduced Hadronic Uncertainty in the Determination of V_ud
status_evidence.snippet: Expresses the hadronic γW-box contribution via a dispersion relation as an integral over the first Nachtmann moment of F_3, updating Δ_R^V.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical framework using Nachtmann moments exists, but is benchmarked against models/data on γW structure functions, not against a direct beta-energy-slope measurement.

status_evidence.title: Radiative Corrections to Neutron and Nuclear Beta Decays Revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Revisits hadronic and nuclear γW-box contributions and their uncertainties.
status_evidence.claim: Active theoretical work continues; no direct experimental measurement of the small energy slope is reported.

status_evidence.title: Radiative corrections to neutron and nuclear β-decays: a serious kinematics problem
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses kinematics and energy-dependent structure of radiative corrections in β decay.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates ongoing theoretical refinement of energy dependence without a direct experimental benchmark of the nuclear γW-box slope.
